Project under review: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management (a RISC-V bare-metal OS lab, SV39 paging, 2 harts, global kernel lock).
The newly written code is in kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c and include/os/mm.h (see `cd /workspace && git diff`).
Everything else in the tree is given/unmodifiable context: init/main.c, arch/riscv/kernel/{entry.S,boot.c,start.S}, arch/riscv/include/pgtable.h, include/os/{sched.h,elf.h,mm.h}, kernel/irq/irq.c, kernel/syscall/syscall.c, drivers/screen.c, test/*.c, tiny_libc/.
Key facts you must verify against the real files rather than assume:
- user ELFs link at 0x10000 but their PT_LOAD segment starts at vaddr 0xf000 (headers included), memsz up to ~0x3e98.
- USER_STACK_ADDR = 0xf00010000, PGDIR_PA = 0x5e000000, kernel window VPN2 = 0x101, KERNEL_MEM_OFFSET = 0xffffffc000000000.
- main.c init_pcb() loads the shell with load_elf(..., get_kva_of) which only WALKS the page table, so init_page_table() must pre-map the code pages.
- main.c's idle loop frees each exited task's kernel stack with free_user_page(kva2pa(kernel_stack_base - PAGE_SIZE)).
- there is no satp switch in entry.S, so scheduler() must do it.
Only report defects in the NEW code. Do not report pre-existing issues in given files unless the new code depends on them incorrectly.

A reviewer claims the following defect in the NEW code. Try hard to REFUTE it by reading the actual files. Default to refuted=true when you cannot demonstrate a concrete failure.

TITLE: write_to_sd copies the victim frame to disk before invalidating its PTE, so concurrent user writes on the other hart are silently lost
FILE: Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/mm/mm.c
CLAIM: write_to_sd() (mm.c:123-149) does `sbi_sd_write(pa, ...)` first (line 134) and only afterwards clears _PAGE_PRESENT / sets _PAGE_SOFT / calls flush_tlb_all() (lines 140-147). The kernel lock (kernel/sched/smp.c:30) is released by ret_from_exception before `sret` (arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S:157), so while hart 0 is inside write_to_sd, hart 1 can be executing user code in the very address space that owns the victim frame. Concrete failure: process P runs on hart 1 with va V -> frame F mapped writable (alloc_page_helper always grants _PAGE_WRITE|_PAGE_DIRTY, mm.c:233). Hart 0 takes a page fault for another task, alloc_user_page (mm.c:60-65) finds no free frame, selete_page() returns F, write_to_sd snapshots F to swap slot i. Hart 1 then stores 0xdead to V — the PTE is still present and its TLB entry is still valid, so the store lands in F. Hart 0 now clears _PAGE_PRESENT, flushes, frees F, memsets it (mm.c:75) and hands it to the new owner. When P later faults on V, alloc_page_helper reads back the pre-store copy from slot i: P's write has vanished with no error. The invalidate+shootdown must happen before the sbi_sd_write, not after. The same window also lets a stale remote TLB entry write into a frame hart 0 has already memset and reassigned to a different process.

input.reason:
REFUTED — the described window cannot open in this build: `write_to_sd()` is unreachable, and the claim is a theoretical ordering nit rather than a demonstrable defect.

1) The swap-out path is dead code in this configuration. `write_to_sd()` is called from exactly one place, `alloc_user_page()` at /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/mm/mm.c:60-63, and only after the linear scan over all `USER_PAGE_NUM` entries fails to find a free frame. `USER_PAGE_NUM = (USER_MEM_END - USER_MEM_BEGIN)/PAGE_SIZE` with the *given, unmodified* constants in /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/include/os/mm.h:50-51 (`0x51000000..0x5e000000`) = 53248 frames = 208 MB. The git diff of mm.h touches only lines 102+ (new prototypes and the SHM/USER_CODE/SD_BLOCK macros); the memory-layout constants are pre-existing context, so the new code cannot be blamed for them.
